steps: 1000px, learner chosen. Start a quiz with a wrong multiple-choice answer (#/quiz?scope=section&id=9.1&count=8&seed=7&templateShare=0.3&openShare=0.2, press a, Enter), Tab to 'Show me the essentials', press Enter
On a worked problem (#/quiz?scope=section&id=1.4&count=6&seed=5&templateShare=0&openShare=1) press Ctrl+Enter, Tab to 'I got it' / 'I missed it', press Enter
Tab to 'Quit to chapters' and to each header link (Stats Trainer, Chapters, Review mistakes, Progress, About) and to 'switch', press Enter on each

New: on a true/false question (#/quiz?scope=section&id=1.2&count=10&seed=295939&templateShare=0.4&openShare=0.3) the True button is auto-focused; press t (or f) and then Enter as the on-screen hint says
expected: Enter activates whatever is focused, and the hint 'Press t or f, Enter to check' is true on a true/false question.
actual: Every case listed in round one is fixed: Enter on 'Show me the essentials' expands the panel (focus moves to 'Hide'), Enter on 'Hide' collapses it, Enter on 'I got it'/'I missed it' records the self-grade and moves focus to 'Next question', Enter on 'Quit to chapters', on all five header links and on 'switch' navigates. But the fix reversed the priority and broke true/false: the focused option button now swallows Enter, so the global check never runs. Press t then Enter: nothing happens at all, however many times you press it. Press f then Enter: focus is still on True (it never follows the selection), so Enter re-selects True and silently replaces the learner's answer of False - still without checking. The only way to check a true/false answer from the keyboard is to Tab to 'Check answer'.

steps: Open http://localhost:3010/#/ at width 400 with no learner, read document.documentElement.scrollWidth
Enter a name, Start, read it again, scroll to the chapter list and read it again

Repeat on chapter/3, chapter/11, section/3.4, section/11.3, progress, review, about, on every question of quizzes for sections 3.4 (seed 42), 11.3 (seed 3), 1.2 (seed 295939), 9.1, 6.1, 1.4 and of the chapter 3 quiz, and on each score page
actual: scrollWidth is 400 on every one of those routes and on all 68 quiz questions walked - home before and after choosing a learner, chapter, section, quiz, score, review, progress, about. Section titles wrap and the status badges are on screen. The only routes that still overflow are the print views, which round one did not test - see finding print-page-overflows-sideways.

steps: Browser 1 at 400px: name 'Persist Tester', take a 5-question quiz to the score page, open Progress and Review (one quiz, four open mistakes)
Browser 2 (separate context, empty storage): same name 'Persist Tester', open Progress and Review
Read the home page and the About page for what they promise
Watch the network log for anything but the page and the Google Fonts stylesheet
expected: The app's promise about where progress lives matches what actually happens.
actual: The promise has been corrected rather than the storage. About now reads 'Progress is saved in this browser only, under your learner name; another browser or device starts fresh.' and the home page makes no claim about a server or another device. The second browser still shows 'No quizzes yet' / 'Nothing to review', and the only requests are the page itself and fonts.googleapis.com - which is now exactly what the app says. No longer misleading.

steps: 1000px, start #/quiz?scope=section&id=1.4&count=6&seed=5&templateShare=0&openShare=1 (all worked problems)
Read the hint under the auto-focused workspace
Type 'a t f b d 4 my answer', press Enter, then Ctrl+Enter
Repeat with Meta+Enter, and separately Tab to 'Show model answer' and press Enter
expected: The hint names the key that actually reveals the model answer.
actual: The hint now reads 'Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on Mac) to see the model answer' and is true: Ctrl+Enter reveals it, Meta+Enter reveals it, Enter inserts a newline (which the hint no longer contradicts), Tab+Enter on 'Show model answer' reveals it. Letters a, t, f, b, d typed into the workspace land as text and are not hijacked as shortcuts.

steps: 1000px: choose a multiple-choice option with a letter key, press Enter, inspect document.activeElement and the .key-hint text
Repeat after checking a numeric, fill-in and true/false answer, and after pressing 'I got it' on a worked problem
Press Enter once more and confirm it advances exactly one question
expected: Focus lands on the way forward and a hint says so.
actual: Fixed at both moments round one named: after every check and after every self-grade focus is on the 'Next question' (or 'Finish') button and the hint reads 'Press Enter for the next question'. One Enter checks, a second Enter advances exactly one question - no double advance in 68 questions across five quizzes. Focus is still dropped to <body> at one other moment, when the model answer is revealed; filed separately as focus-lost-after-model-answer.

steps: 400px and 1000px: start a multiple-choice, a true/false and a numeric quiz and tap 'Check answer' with nothing chosen / an empty field
Repeat by pressing Enter instead of tapping
expected: A message such as 'Choose an answer first'.
actual: 'Choose an answer first.' now appears next to the button in all six cases at both widths, whether the button is tapped or Enter is pressed, and focus stays on the button. The one gap is true/false by Enter: Enter never reaches the check at all (it selects True instead), so no message appears - see the enter-hijacks-focused-controls row.

steps: Open #/quiz?scope=section&id=1.2&count=10&seed=295939&templateShare=0.4&openShare=0.3 at 400px and 1000px, in the light and the dark scheme
Look at True/False before pressing anything, then choose one and look again
expected: Neither option looks chosen until the learner picks one.
actual: Fixed. Unchosen and focused, True reads 'True' with the normal border and background and only a 2px accent outline; chosen, it reads '✓ True' with an accent border and a tinted fill (light rgb(224,238,240) / dark rgb(28,51,56)). The tick makes the two states unmistakable in both schemes at both widths. aria-pressed tracks the selection correctly.

steps: At 400px open #/quiz?scope=section&id=11.3&count=10&seed=3&templateShare=0.5&openShare=0.3 and advance to question 2 (a 642px-wide table in a 332px box), in the light scheme and then in the dark scheme
Look at the right edge of the table, scroll the table fully right and look at both edges
expected: A visible cue in both schemes that the table scrolls sideways, and no cue at an edge that has nothing more to show.
actual: A 14px edge fade has been added and it behaves correctly: at scrollLeft 0 the right edge is shaded and the left is clean, fully scrolled right the left edge is shaded and the right is clean, and the page itself never scrolls sideways (scrollWidth stays 400). But it is only visible in the light scheme - sampled pixels go 253 -> 214 in light (clearly visible) and only 27 -> 23 in dark, a 4/255 step that is invisible on the dark background round one tested in. A dark-scheme learner still has no cue, and in the 3.4 question the column the stem asks about stays hidden until they guess to swipe.

steps: Open the home page, a chapter page and a section page at width 400 after choosing a learner
Measure the 'switch' button, the header links and the count / worked-problem selects
actual: 'switch' grew from 38x16 to 54x24 but is still well under 40px tall; the header links are unchanged at 20px tall (Chapters 63x20, Review mistakes 117x20, Progress 60x20, About 41x20, Stats Trainer 92x24); the selects are unchanged at 28px tall (questions 56x28, worked problems 86x28). The new 'Print OpenStax Final Exam' links on the home page are 225x30. Quiz controls are fine (options 42-62px, Check/Next 44px, True/False 46px, workspace 142px).

steps: At 1000px open #/quiz?scope=section&id=1.2&count=10&seed=295939&templateShare=0.4&openShare=0.3 - question 1 is true/false and the True button is auto-focused
The hint under the buttons reads 'Press t or f, Enter to check'. Press t, then press Enter (twice, three times)
Reload fresh and instead press f, then press Enter
As a keyboard-only learner, try to get the answer checked without the mouse
expected: Enter checks the answer, exactly as the hint says, whichever option is chosen.
actual: Enter is swallowed by the focused option button and the check never runs. After 't' the button under focus is the one already chosen, so Enter re-selects it and nothing at all happens - no feedback, no 'Choose an answer first', no focus change, forever. After 'f' focus is still on True (it never follows the selection), so Enter selects True: the learner's answer of False is silently replaced by the opposite answer and still nothing is checked. The only way through is to Tab to 'Check answer' (2 Tab presses) and press Enter there, which nothing on screen mentions. Hit on every true/false question in the 1.2 quiz and in the chapter 3 quiz.

steps: At 1000px start #/quiz?scope=section&id=1.4&count=6&seed=5&templateShare=0&openShare=1 (worked problems only)
Type an answer in the workspace and press Ctrl+Enter (or Tab to 'Show model answer' and press Enter)
Inspect document.activeElement and the .key-hint text, then count the Tab presses needed to reach 'I got it'
expected: After the model answer appears, focus lands on 'I got it' (or the panel) and a hint names the key that grades it - the same courtesy the app now shows after a check.
actual: Focus is dropped to <body> and the key-hint area goes empty, so a keyboard learner is thrown back to the top of the tab cycle: 'I got it' is 7-8 Tab presses away, through the whole header, on every worked problem. Reproduced on all 22 worked problems in sections 1.4, 9.1, 1.2, 6.1 and the chapter 3 quiz. Both buttons work once reached (Enter and Space).

steps: Choose a learner, open chapter 3, tap 'Print chapter test' (#/print?scope=chapter&id=3&count=15&seed=4) at width 400
Read document.documentElement.scrollWidth; repeat at 1000px and with print media emulated; also #/print?scope=section&id=3.4&count=10&seed=2 and #/print?scope=final&id=1&count=100&seed=1
expected: The printable test fits the sheet at any width, as every other route now does.
actual: Print views are the one place that still scrolls sideways: scrollWidth 1175 for the chapter 3 test at 400px (546 for the 3.4 section test, 482 for Final Exam 1) and 1275 at 1000px, 1251 with print media emulated. A contingency table in the answer key is 1099px wide inside a 1024px sheet, so it hangs 75px past the paper edge and ~340px past a 1000px window - on paper the right-hand columns are cut off. On a phone the learner has to pan the whole sheet sideways to read any of it.

steps: Open #/print?scope=chapter&id=3&count=15&seed=4 and #/print?scope=chapter&id=11&count=15&seed=6
Read the answer key at the bottom (items 11 in chapter 3, two items in chapter 11)
expected: The answer key shows the answer parts, not the markup that produced them.
actual: Raw '[PARTS]' and '[/PARTS]' markers are printed in the answer key - two in the chapter 3 test, four in the chapter 11 test. The parts inside them also run together on one line instead of being listed. The on-screen quiz does not show these markers (10 chapter 3 questions checked), so it is the print view only.

steps: At 400px in the dark scheme open #/quiz?scope=section&id=11.3&count=10&seed=3&templateShare=0.5&openShare=0.3 and advance to question 2
Look at the right edge of the wide table, then sample the pixels there and compare with the light scheme
expected: The new edge fade reads as a cue in the dark scheme too.
actual: The fade is drawn in both schemes (four background gradients on .table-scroll, 14px wide, correctly hidden at whichever edge has nothing more to show), but in dark it is only a 4/255 step - rgb(27,36,41) to rgb(23,31,35) - which is invisible; in light the same cue is a 39/255 step (253 to 214) and reads clearly. Dark-scheme phone learners still get a flat clipped edge.

steps: At 1000px start #/quiz?scope=section&id=6.1&count=8&seed=11&templateShare=0.5&openShare=0.2 (question 1 is numeric, field auto-focused)
Type 'abtfd' - the letters are not hijacked as shortcuts, which is right - then press Enter
expected: A field that only takes numbers either refuses the letters or says the answer is not a number; a typo should not cost the learner the question.
actual: The field accepts 'abtfd-12.5e3' as-is and Enter grades it 'Not quite.', spending the question and adding a mistake to the review log, with no hint that the entry was not a number. (The 'Choose an answer first.' message the build now shows for an empty field would be the natural thing to reuse.)

steps: At 1000px start #/quiz?scope=section&id=9.1&count=8&seed=7&templateShare=0.3&openShare=0.2 and reach question 3 (fill in H0 and Ha)
With the first blank focused, Tab towards the second blank and count the presses
expected: Tab moves from one blank to the next.
actual: The second blank is 7 Tab presses away: Tab walks through that row's six symbol buttons (=, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥) first. Typing '!=' into the blanks works and Enter from either blank does check the answer, so the question is completable, but filling both blanks by keyboard is clumsy.
